description: Machine-validated registry of the repository's hard rules. This file is NOT auto-loaded by agent harnesses; AGENTS.md is the always-loaded system prompt. The constitution exists so every recurring rule is tied to real enforcement, cannot silently rot into documentation, and can be validated by scripts/quality/audit-constitution.mjs. Roles in .ai/roles/ are on-demand task personas; load AGENTS.md -> canonical doc -> one role -> at most one skill.

rules.title: No emoji anywhere
rules.statement: Source, docs, UI strings, commit messages and generated artifacts contain no emoji. Use Lucide/Phosphor icons instead.

rules.title: 400-line source budget, shrink-only baseline
rules.statement: Hand-maintained source files are capped at 400 lines. Frozen over-cap files may shrink but never grow; split before extending. Untracked WIP is reported, never frozen.

rules.title: IPC seam is typed and name-checked
rules.statement: Every TypeScript invoke names a real registered Tauri command, payloads cross the seam through varve-bridge/serde structs, and new commands do not use serde_json::Value. Adopt the phased tauri-specta plan.

rules.title: Agent surface stays fixed
rules.statement: AGENTS.md stays within 150 lines / 9000 bytes, the three ignore files stay byte-identical and keep their required patterns, and every Read-next pointer resolves.

rules.title: Compact repo map cannot drift
rules.statement: docs/agents/repo-map.generated.md is generated from the committed tree and must be regenerated with pnpm agent:map in the same change as a structural move; never hand-edit it.

rules.title: Documentation index, links and current naming
rules.statement: Current-state docs do not reference dead names or paths, every relative markdown link resolves, and the ADR index is complete.

rules.title: TypeScript strict and lint-clean
rules.statement: No explicit any, strict TypeScript, and Biome lint/format rules hold across the workspace.

rules.title: Client trust boundaries
rules.statement: Client builds consume only the documented client-safe env allowlist; no private credential class, signing or backend secret enters a client build.

rules.title: No secrets in source or artifacts
rules.statement: Credentials, tokens, keys and account material never enter the repository or shipped artifacts; secret scanning fails closed.

rules.title: Import boundaries between apps and packages
rules.statement: Apps never import other apps or the future backend; packages never import apps; shared code lives in packages/.

rules.title: Hub import budgets and complexity ceilings
rules.statement: Hub files (Shell, CanvasArea, Menubar, context, HomeShell) may not gain imports without removing equal weight; complexity ceilings block growth, and over-ceiling files carry a first-line COMPLEXITY comment.

rules.title: No dependency cycles or layer violations
rules.statement: Workspace dependency cycles keep their known identities, the global cycle ceiling holds, and cross-layer imports are rejected.

rules.title: No AI-tool attribution in commits
rules.statement: Commit messages and author metadata carry no AI-tool trailers, signatures or generated-by lines; the maintainer authors all commits.

rules.title: Never show pixels no fresh frame will replace
rules.statement: Any partial/dirty-rect/camera-fast-path reuse is a loan against an authoritative frame. Worker refusals must be synchronously decidable; when no fresh frame is coming, fall back to the full replay. Prove pixel-reuse changes with the forceFullRedraw hash oracle.

checklist: Read docs/architecture/render-pipeline.md -> 'Reuse of already-painted pixels'.
Every worker-refusal path is decidable synchronously before the branch paints.
Hash the surface after the interaction, call window.__varvePerf.forceFullRedraw() at the same camera, hash again; unequal hashes fail review.

rules.title: Operator-owned state stays out of the repository
rules.statement: Never commit or overwrite runtime state, credentials, docs evidence/screenshots, lockfiles, generated data tables, vendored sources, or another session's uncommitted work. Read them only through exact paths when a task requires it.

checklist: git status/diff reviewed: no unrelated or other-session files staged.
No lockfile, vendor/, generated data table, docs artifacts/screenshots or runtime state staged.
Any intentional --force baseline re-adoption is justified in the same change.

rules.title: Validation runs through the shared queue
rules.statement: Local agents do not each run independent gates on the workstation. Use the queued scripts (check:agent, check:rust, test:agent, verify:affected, verify:agent); the queue serializes exclusive lanes and hands back clean-tree receipts.

checklist: Gate commands were the queued package scripts, not raw tsc/cargo/vitest runs.
Receipt output (pass/duration/path) was recorded in the validation report.
Any bypass (CI, VARVE_VALIDATION_QUEUE=0) was deliberate and stated.

rules.title: Button and control vocabulary is closed
rules.statement: Actions use @varve/ui Button/IconButton/ToggleButton; hand-rolled varve-btn markup, undeclared modifiers, native <select>, and invented variants fail the system tests.

rules.title: Regressions fail against previous behavior
rules.statement: Every observed defect gets a regression test that fails before the fix, asserts real outcomes, and uses production contracts; cancellation, invalid-input, permission, timing, persistence and platform cases are covered where relevant.

checklist: Regression test written first and observed failing on the previous behavior.
Test asserts outcome/contract, not implementation details or weakened mocks.
Affected closure rerun and results recorded in the Agent Validation Report.

rules.title: External agent tooling is pinned, sandboxed and verified
rules.statement: Code-graph/MCP servers and other external agent tooling are not default dependencies. Adoption requires a pinned version, sandboxed execution, and output verified against the generated repository map; it never replaces exact file/line reads for edits.

checklist: Any adopted tool is version-pinned and recorded in the dependency/config review.
The tool runs with the repository (not the host) as its trust boundary and without credentials.
Its structural output agrees with docs/agents/repo-map.generated.md; differences are explained or the tool is rejected.
Exact file/line reads remain the source of truth for edits.

rules.title: Concurrent work uses worktrees, single-writer surfaces and staged validation
rules.statement: Parallel agents isolate with one worktree per task, never share a worktree writer, serialize generated surfaces (AGENTS/indexes, lockfiles, baselines, generated map/CSS, ignore trios), and judge commits on staged content. Merges are sequential and validated before and after.

checklist: This task writes files in its own worktree; no second writer shares the checkout.
Any generated surface touched by two sides was regenerated after the merge, not hand-merged.
The commit used staged-only validators (agent map --staged, file-size --staged, health --staged) rather than attributing another session's dirty tree.
Merges ran pnpm verify:plan and pnpm verify:affected; stale worktrees were pruned only with worktree:prune after being clean and merged.

rules.title: Visual baselines are reviewed, scoped and single-writer
rules.statement: An intended design change updates visual baselines only through the scoped pnpm visual:update wrapper for one spec/project with a stated reason; regressions are fixed instead of accepted; text-raster drift inside a documented budget is not a design change; baselines are never hand-merged or updated by broad --update-snapshots runs.

checklist: The failing spec/project was reproduced read-only under the heavy-task lease and classified as intended change vs regression vs environment drift.
If updated, only the intended spec/project baselines changed, a reason was recorded in reports/visual-baseline-updates/ and the commit message, and pnpm audit:visual-baselines passes.
No broad --update-snapshots run, no hand-merged PNG, and no tolerance raised without a measured explanation.
